title: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree
summary: Kuinka before an adjective asks about degree: Kuinka vanha olet? Kuinka vanha sinä olet? — Olen kaksikymmentä vuotta vanha.
targetSkills: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree
prerequisiteSkills: Miten and kuinka: answering about manner
objectives: Ask about degree with kuinka and an adjective.
Give the requested age or measurement using the provided expressions.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.

Kuinka before an adjective asks about degree: Kuinka vanha olet? (“How old are you?”) and Kuinka pitkä matka on? (“How long is the journey?”). Miten is possible in several such patterns; these tasks teach the neutral kuinka pattern and accept a natural miten alternative.
keyPoints: Kuinka plus an adjective asks for degree, not a reason.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Give the requested age or measurement, using the provided complete expression. Olen kaksikymmentä vuotta vanha means I am twenty years old. Matka on kaksi kilometriä means the journey is two kilometres long. Another age pattern uses -vuotias, but its formation is outside this bounded target.
A natural short reply to “Kuinka vanha sinä olet?” is “Kaksikymmentä vuotta.” (“Twenty years old.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
A degree correction rejects an incorrect age and supplies the correct one. The complete negative phrase en ole and both number expressions are shown here.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Give the requested degree or measurement, not a manner adverb such as hyvin.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: vuotta means years here. Vuosi has the singular partitive vuotta, used after the supplied numbers greater than one.
kilometriä means kilometres here. Kilometri + -ä gives singular partitive kilometriä after a number greater than one.
sivua means pages here. Sivu + -a gives singular partitive sivua after the supplied number.
senttimetriä means centimetres here. Senttimetri + -ä gives the supplied singular partitive senttimetriä after the number.

steps: Kuinka: how; question asking the degree of a quality. Kuinka asks about manner or, before an adjective, degree.
vanha: old; quality whose degree is being asked about. Vanha is the basic singular adjective meaning old.
sinä: you; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Sinä addresses one person informally.
olet: you are; verb (the action or state). Olla has the singular you-form olet: ole- + -t.
Olen: I am; verb (the action or state). Olla has the I-form olen: ole- + -n. The ending identifies the speaker.
kaksikymmentä: twenty; number in the requested measurement. Kaksikymmentä is the supplied complete number twenty.
vuotta: years; measurement describing the subject. Vuosi has the singular partitive vuotta, used after the supplied numbers greater than one.
vanha: old; description of what the subject is like. Vanha is the basic singular adjective meaning old.
Kuinka: how; question asking the degree of a quality. Kuinka asks about manner or, before an adjective, degree.
pitkä: tall or long; quality whose degree is being asked about. Pitkä describes a person's height or a thing's length; context determines tall or long.
matka: journey; subject (who or what this sentence is about). Matka is the basic noun meaning journey; its length can answer kuinka pitkä.
on: is; verb (the action or state). Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.

steps: En: I do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). En is the first-person singular negative verb. The main verb takes its negative form.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
